rules.name: Artifact logging configuration needs review
rules.short_description: dbt_artifacts has an upload hook with disabled models, or the package is installed without that hook.
rules.long_description:
dbt_artifacts requires its storage tables and upload hook to be configured for the installed package version. A hook can fail if its target tables were never created or no longer match the package schema. A missing hook can leave runs unrecorded.

This rule reviews disabled package models or a missing hook. Disabled marts do not always mean broken logging: the package documents a setup with marts disabled and raw source models enabled. Tables may also be managed separately. Check effective configuration and actual uploads before changing it.

## References

- [dbt Artifacts Package](https://github.com/brooklyn-data/dbt_artifacts)
rules.remediation: Follow the installed package version's setup and upgrade instructions. Enable the models that create the required storage tables, install dependencies, and build those tables. Configure the upload_results hook only for the intended targets. If you intentionally keep custom marts, preserve the documented sources-only setup. To disable uploads, remove or gate the hook; do not re-enable every package model without reviewing the design.

examples.title: on-run-end uploads artifacts but the package is disabled
examples.bad:
# dbt_project.yml
on-run-end:
  - "{{ dbt_artifacts.upload_results(results) }}"
models:
  dbt_artifacts:
    +enabled: false

rules.name: Literal credential in project configuration
rules.short_description: A credential field contains a literal value rather than an environment-variable reference.
rules.long_description:
A real credential stored in a project file can be exposed through commits, shared artifacts, or backups. Deleting it from the working tree does not revoke the credential or remove earlier copies.

The rule scans credential fields in local profile and project configuration. It does not prove that the value is secret or that Git tracks the file. Review placeholders without exposing their values. dbt supports env_var in profiles; secret-prefixed variables have extra restrictions and log masking.

## References

- [About env_var function](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/dbt-jinja-functions/env_var)
rules.remediation: If the value is a real credential, revoke or rotate it through the approved secret-management process. Move connection credentials to the appropriate dbt profile or platform connection. In profiles.yml, use an environment variable, preferably with the DBT_ENV_SECRET_ prefix where supported, and inject it securely at run time. Do not use secret-prefixed variables in dbt_project.yml; dbt disallows them there. Remove exposed copies under the repository's incident procedure. Treat documented non-secret placeholders separately.

rules.name: Evaluator primary-key test configuration needs review
rules.short_description: dbt_project_evaluator has no explicit primary_key_test_macros setting for project-specific key tests.
rules.long_description:
dbt_project_evaluator uses primary_key_test_macros to decide which test combinations establish key coverage. Its documented defaults include unique with not_null, and dbt_utils.unique_combination_of_columns. They do not automatically cover every package's key tests.

This rule reports a missing explicit setting when the evaluator package is installed. It does not prove that dbt_constraints is used or that a reported key gap is false. Keep the defaults when they already match the project's tests.

## References

- [Overriding Variables](https://dbt-labs.github.io/dbt-project-evaluator/latest/customization/overriding-variables/)
rules.remediation: Check the installed evaluator version and the tests applied to model keys. If the project uses dbt_constraints, add its relevant test macros to vars.dbt_project_evaluator.primary_key_test_macros. Each accepted alternative must be a list of project_name.test_macro_name values; keep required test combinations together. Preserve applicable defaults when overriding the list, and rerun the evaluator to check the result.

rules.name: Separate dbt run and test steps
rules.short_description: A script or workflow invokes dbt run and dbt test as separate steps.
rules.long_description:
dbt run builds models without running data tests. If all models run before tests, downstream models can consume an upstream result before its tests fail. dbt build orders selected models and tests through the dependency graph and can skip downstream work after blocking test failures.

Blocking depends on test severity, selection, and multi-parent dependencies. A successful build verifies the selected operations and assertions, not all business logic. Separate steps can remain appropriate when their ordering and purpose are deliberate.

## References

- [About dbt build command](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/commands/build)
rules.remediation: Consider one dbt build command for the intended resource selection. Check selectors, exclusions, test severity, hooks, and any seed or snapshot behavior before replacing the existing commands. Run the revised workflow in a controlled target. Keep separate steps when they serve a documented need and have adequate failure handling.

rules.name: Metrics hook and table materialization on a folder
rules.short_description: A non-mart folder has an m_register_* post-hook and a table materialization setting.
rules.long_description:
The rule detects a local conversion-instrumentation pattern: a folder-level m_register_* post-hook beside materialized: table outside marts. A post-hook runs after a model is built; inherited configuration can therefore add work to many models.

The pattern does not prove that the hook writes data or that it caused the table setting. dbt supports both hooks and folder materialization settings. Review their combined cost and purpose before removing them.

## References

- [pre-hook & post-hook](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/resource-configs/pre-hook-post-hook)
- [on-run-start & on-run-end](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/project-configs/on-run-start-on-run-end)
- [Materializations](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/materializations)
rules.remediation: Inspect the metrics macro and the effective materialization for each model in the folder. Remove temporary instrumentation only after preserving needed validation evidence. Restore the materializations chosen for those models. If run-level logging can replace model-level metrics, evaluate an on-run-end hook; the available context and timing differ. Keep production metrics when their purpose and cost are accepted.

rules.name: Run hook contains DDL or DML
rules.short_description: An on-run-start or on-run-end hook contains DDL/DML, directly or in a called macro.
rules.long_description:
dbt explicitly supports SQL and SQL-producing macros in run hooks, including operational DDL. Such work is not a separately selectable model node with its own dependency and test lifecycle. Business transformations placed there can therefore be harder to reason about.

This local review rule exempts dbt_artifacts uploads. It assigns warning-level findings to literal SQL and informational findings to macro calls. A macro wrapper alone does not make an operation safer. Keep justified setup, grants, or logging in hooks.

## References

- [on-run-start & on-run-end](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/project-configs/on-run-start-on-run-end)
- [About dbt run-operation command](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/commands/run-operation)
rules.remediation: Put persistent data transformations in models when that expresses their dependencies correctly. For a separate administrative action, consider an explicit dbt run-operation macro and arrange its ordering in orchestration. run-operation does not add a model node or automatic test dependency. Keep appropriate operational hooks and document their side effects and retry behavior.

rules.name: Runtime function builds dbt variables
rules.short_description: An EXECUTE DBT PROJECT command passes vars assembled from a function result at run time.
rules.long_description:
The rule detects orchestration SQL that builds --vars from a function result before EXECUTE DBT PROJECT. Variables can legitimately differ by run, but the same project code can then produce different SQL or select different inputs. Reproducing a run requires its variable values as well as its code version.

dbt supports runtime variables. This rule is a local reproducibility review, not a ban on them. Keep intentional per-run inputs with documented meaning, validation, and an audit record that excludes secrets.

## References

- [Project variables](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/project-variables)
- [EXECUTE DBT PROJECT](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/sql/execute-dbt-project)
rules.remediation: Put stable defaults in dbt_project.yml or the default argument of var(). For necessary per-run values, validate names and types, serialize them with a structured format, and preserve a non-secret record of the resolved inputs. Check quoting when constructing the orchestration command. Verify argument support for the deployed dbt and Snowflake execution versions.
